topic: Maximum power transfer in a DC resistor network
statement: A battery with electromotive force V_0 and internal resistance r_0 is connected in series with a fixed resistor R_1. The outer terminals of this series combination are connected across a parallel arrangement of a fixed resistor R_2 and a variable load resistor. Determine the maximum power that can be dissipated in the variable load resistor as its resistance is varied over all positive values.

R_1.desc: Resistance of the series fixed resistor

R_2.desc: Resistance of the parallel fixed resistor

statement: A real battery with electromotive force V_0 and internal resistance r_0 is connected in series with a resistor of resistance R_1 and a parallel combination of two resistors of resistances R_2 and R_3. Determine the power dissipated in the resistor of resistance R_2.

R_2.desc: resistance of the first parallel resistor

R_3.desc: resistance of the second parallel resistor

topic: One-dimensional kinematics with constant acceleration and pursuit
statement: A speeder passes a stationary police car while moving along a straight road at a constant speed v_s. After a reaction delay t_r following the instant the speeder passes, the police car starts from rest and pursues the speeder with a constant acceleration of magnitude a_p. Find the distance the police car travels from its starting point until it overtakes the speeder.

t_r.desc: reaction delay before the police car begins accelerating

a_p.desc: magnitude of the constant acceleration of the police car

topic: Standing waves on a string under tension
statement: A uniform string of length L and mass m_s is fixed at both ends and held taut by a hanging block of mass M_h suspended over a frictionless pulley in a uniform gravitational field of acceleration magnitude g. When the string oscillates in a standing wave of harmonic number n, find the frequency of the standing wave.

L.desc: length of the vibrating segment of the string

m_s.desc: mass of the vibrating segment of the string

M_h.desc: mass of the hanging block providing tension

solver_expression: n / (2 * L) * sqrt(M_h * g * L / m_s)

topic: Bernoulli's equation, continuity, and projectile motion from a pressurized tank
statement: A cylindrical tank with uniform horizontal cross-sectional area A_1 rests on a flat horizontal floor. The tank contains an incompressible, inviscid fluid of density rho filled to a height H above the floor. The sealed space above the fluid surface is filled with gas maintained at a constant gauge pressure P_g relative to the surrounding atmosphere. A horizontal nozzle of cross-sectional area A_2 (where A_2 < A_1) opens in the side of the tank at a height y_0 above the floor (where y_0 < H), allowing a steady jet of fluid to exit into the atmosphere under uniform gravitational acceleration g. Neglecting air resistance and viscous effects, find the horizontal distance from the nozzle exit to the point where the fluid jet strikes the floor.

A_1.desc: horizontal cross-sectional area of the tank

A_2.desc: cross-sectional area of the nozzle exit

H.desc: height of the fluid surface above the floor

y_0.desc: height of the nozzle exit above the floor

P_g.desc: gauge pressure of the gas above the fluid surface

topic: standing waves on a string with a submerged hanging mass
statement: A uniform string of linear mass density mu is fixed at one end to a rigid wall and extends horizontally a distance L to a small frictionless pulley. The string passes over the pulley and is attached to a solid block of mass M and density rho_b that hangs vertically and is completely submerged in a stationary liquid of density rho_f (with rho_b > rho_f). Assume the mass of the vertical segment of the string is negligible compared to M so that the tension in the horizontal segment is uniform, and treat the wall and the pulley as fixed nodes. Find the fundamental frequency of standing waves on the horizontal segment of the string, given gravitational acceleration g.

mu.desc: linear mass density of the string

L.desc: length of the horizontal segment of the string between the wall and the pulley

rho_f.desc: density of the liquid in which the block is submerged

answer_expression: sqrt(M * g * (1 - rho_f / rho_b) / mu) / (2 * L)

statement: A small bob is attached to one end of a light, inextensible string of length L, while the other end is fixed to a ceiling pivot. The bob moves in a horizontal circle at a constant speed so that the string sweeps out a cone and maintains a constant angle theta with the vertical. Given that the magnitude of the gravitational acceleration is g, determine the period of the bob's circular motion.

theta.desc: constant angle between the string and the vertical

g.desc: magnitude of the acceleration due to gravity

statement: A conical pendulum consists of a small bob of mass m attached to one end of a light, inextensible string of length L, with the other end fixed to a rigid pivot. In a region with uniform downward gravitational acceleration g, the bob revolves at a constant speed v in a horizontal circle centered vertically below the pivot. Find the magnitude of the tension in the string.

topic: ballistic pendulum with a massive rod
statement: A ballistic pendulum consists of a uniform rigid rod of mass m_r and length L, pivoted frictionlessly at its upper end, with a small target block of mass m_p attached to its lower end. Initially, the pendulum hangs vertically at rest. A bullet of mass m_b, moving horizontally at speed v_0, strikes the target block and becomes embedded in it. As a result, the pendulum swings upward to a maximum angle theta from the vertical (with theta < pi). Assuming uniform gravitational acceleration g and negligible collision duration, find the initial speed v_0 of the bullet.

m_p.desc: mass of the target block at the lower end of the rod

m_r.desc: mass of the uniform rigid rod

L.desc: length of the rod from the pivot to the target block

theta.desc: maximum swing angle measured from the downward vertical

answer_expression: sqrt(2*g*L*(1 - cos(theta))*(m_b + m_p + m_r/3)*(m_b + m_p + m_r/2))/m_b

statement: An object is placed at a distance d_o in front of a diverging thin lens whose focal length has magnitude f. Find the magnitude of the distance from the lens to the resulting virtual image.

d_o.desc: distance from the object to the diverging thin lens

f.desc: magnitude of the focal length of the diverging thin lens

topic: Two-block inclined plane system with kinetic friction
statement: A block of mass m1 is placed on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle theta with the horizontal, where the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is mu_k. The block is connected by a light, inextensible string passing over a massless, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass m2. The system is released from rest in a uniform gravitational field of acceleration g, and m2 is sufficiently large that m1 accelerates up the incline. Find the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended a vertical distance d.

m1.desc: Mass of the block on the inclined plane

theta.desc: Angle of the inclined plane above the horizontal

mu_k.desc: Coefficient of kinetic friction between block m1 and the inclined plane

d.desc: Vertical distance descended by the hanging block

statement: A small bob is attached to the end of a light, inextensible string of length L fixed at its upper end. The bob moves in a horizontal circle as a conical pendulum such that the string makes a constant angle theta (less than pi/2) with the vertical, in a uniform gravitational field of magnitude g. Find the period of the bob's circular motion.

theta.desc: angle of the string from the vertical

statement: A uniform horizontal circular disk of mass M and radius R rotates freely without friction about a fixed vertical axis through its center with initial angular speed omega_i. A small object of mass m is dropped vertically from rest just above the disk and sticks to its surface at a distance r from the rotation axis. Find the magnitude of the final angular speed of the combined disk-and-object system.

M.desc: mass of the uniform circular disk

R.desc: radius of the uniform circular disk

omega_i.desc: initial angular speed of the disk

m.desc: mass of the small object dropped onto the disk

r.desc: radial distance from the rotation axis at which the object sticks
